title: Tree items need an accessible name
summary: An element with role="treeitem" has no text or label. Give each tree item visible text or an aria-label so screen readers can announce it.
problem: An element with role="treeitem", such as an entry in a file browser or nested menu, has no text content, aria-label or aria-labeledby. Assistive technology can announce its position in the tree but not what it is.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users moving through a tree hear "tree item" with no name, so they cannot tell folders or pages apart. Voice control users cannot name an item to select it.
whyItMatters: This is a recommended practice rather than a WCAG failure, because many tree widgets name their items already. Where one does not, the whole tree becomes unusable for people who rely on names to navigate it.
steps: Find the element with role="treeitem" in the scan result.
Put the item's text inside it, such as the folder or page name. That text becomes its name.
If the visible text sits elsewhere, point to it with aria-labeledby, or add an aria-label to the item.
Check that icons inside the item have aria-hidden="true" so only the name is announced.
howToCheck: Select each tree item in the browser accessibility inspector and read its Name. Every item should have a distinct, meaningful name. An empty Name means the item is unnamed.
